method: Routed all 110 source-action observations to 35 document-specific historical event-context clusters; 31 high-value cross-source relationships read and classified manually using catalogue action descriptions, occasion and regional/period scope. These are review labels not original historical manuscript comparisons or independent corroboration. Flag two same-author inter-volume repetitions. Source observation count unchanged.

comparisons.rationale: Forty Hours is a wider Eucharistic devotion: a September Rosalia grotto occurrence is not Weiser's pre-Lenten timing; this is not source corroboration of one annual practice.
Kneeling as the Eucharist passes is similar devotional posture to adoration by a home; Palermo historic street procession and a different generic example are not proved the same local custom.
Bodily penitential disciplines within confraternities are not automatically the public hooded-confraternity procession; participation and ritual action differ.
The two-day bread-and-water fasting motif is close to the Handbook historical Passion fast, but setting, date, practice-lineage and historical sources need exact comparison.
Avoiding carriage journeys in historic Palermo is not refraining from television or entertainment on Good Friday.
A reported Palermo decree changing Corpus Christi morning-to-afternoon procession in 1782 is not the Basque Octave Sunday programme.
Palermo's recurring civic vow to the Immaculate Conception is not equivalent to broad Marian novenas or processions in the Handbook.
Jewellery on a processional Marian statue in December differs from May crowning of a domestic Marian statue.
Assumption guild cilii depicting saints' lives are not the Roussillon Holy Week misteri representing Passion scenes; generic shoulder carriage only.
Palermo silver Immaculate Conception statue is not a claimed Marian hair relic carried in Palmi.
St Bartholomew charity brothers travel to a hospital with new shirts and lint, unlike the Enna Holy Wednesday Addolorata cortege.
A historic pledge about defending Mary's Immaculate Conception is not a novena or generic feast procession.
A craft guild ceasing work on its corporate patron's day is not a child's baptismal patronal name day.
Funeral bells cannot be identified with Easter bells from a single shared noun.
The imposition of ashes is a liturgical rite; the Kelly family recommendation to attend it does not establish two local customs.
Guild saint statues in historical Palermo and saint relics/statues at a Breton pardon are related acts but distinct local traditions.
Sawing a Lent figure in Ballarò marketplace may resemble winter effigy processions, but season, material, social meaning and region need verification.
Joseph of Arimathea burial almsgiving is neither St Joseph the Foster Father nor household St Joseph tables.
Ascension seaside livestock washing with protective folk belief is not decorating livestock for a local animal blessing at a Breton pardon.
St Anthony Abbot animal blessing occurs in both Palermo and Salemi descriptions, but centuries/localities differ; separate historical witnesses and local variants are not yet demonstrated.
The Palermo report mentions animal blessing but not the barley/oats/beans mixture described at Salemi. Do not transfer materials across towns.
Burial of executed prisoners by La Sanch brothers is not identical to the Joseph of Arimathea confraternity's collecting alms for pauper burial.
The Marian eight-night pilgrimage is unrelated to eight nights of Holy Souls devotion after All Souls.
The Palermo civic visit to the Rosalia shrine during Forty Hours is not the Weiser pre-Lenten Forty Hours devotion.
Multiple Masses for a dead noble's suffrages are not Mexican Holy Thursday visiting several churches.
Burial under one's confraternity chapel differs from interment wearing a confraternity penitential robe; neither verifies the other's region or period.
Lenten sermons in Palermo's principal church are not weekday Mass attendance during Lent.
Pitrè's patronal guild Mass and Gubbio masons' re-established feast Mass resemble a genre of action; guild and chronology are distinct.
Palermo craft guild patron saint system differs from Sassari gremi each maintaining a processional Candeliere and saint.
Reciting rosary on historic Palermo's eight-night Marian pilgrimage is not a generic family evening Rosary.
Palermo civic officials swearing a Marian historical oath are not a family renewing baptismal promises on Holy Saturday.

same_author_repeated_components.interpretation: Both volume passages describe Senate participation at St Rosalia's sanctuary Forty Hours, likely same author describing one historical devotional setting; not two independent witnesses.
Both volume passages describe Assumption guild ceri/cilii offerings; same author and city, so second passage is not independent historical corroboration.
